hyperedges.label: GitHub Actions CI Pipeline (lint/test gate build, parallel type check)
End-to-End Ticket Polling Flow (macOS app → Next.js API → Jira → PostgreSQL)
Clean Code Standards Enforcement (slash commands scaffold and audit against shared line limits)

nodes.label: File Size Line Limits (100/300/250/200)
nodes.rationale: Files exceeding line limits signal mixed concerns; the command prescribes refactoring routes into services, splitting services by feature, and extracting sub-components. Note: uses looser limits (100/300/250/200) than clean-code-standards (80/250/200/150), indicating a stale or legacy limit set.

nodes.label: Critical File Size Limits (80/250/200/100/150)
nodes.rationale: Hard per-file-type line limits (API route 80, service 250, component 200, hook 100, utility 150, function 30) enforce single responsibility; the rule 'if > 80% of limit, refactor first' front-loads refactoring before code is added. Based on Clean Code, Bulletproof React, and Rule of 30.

nodes.label: Thin Route → Service → Repository Pattern
nodes.rationale: Requests flow API Route (thin) → Service (logic) → Repository (data), with lib utils holding external API clients; keeping HTTP handling separate from business logic keeps routes testable and under the 80-line limit.

nodes.label: Five-Layer Architecture (Client/API/Service/Repository/Data)
nodes.rationale: Client (React/Zustand/TanStack Query) → API (Next.js routes + tRPC) → Service (business logic + integrations) → Repository (Prisma wrapper) → Data (PostgreSQL); each layer only talks to the one below, isolating framework, logic, and persistence concerns.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern (server/repository)
nodes.rationale: Seven repositories abstract Prisma access from business logic and convert snake_case DB rows to camelCase domain types (toDomain), so services never depend on Prisma column naming.

nodes.label: Challenge-Based Mutation Security
nodes.rationale: Protected mutations require a server-issued challenge token, client proof-of-work, a one-time nonce (replay prevention), and a request hash (integrity), sent as X-Challenge-* headers; PoW deters bots without user accounts.

nodes.label: Purely Polling-Based Architecture
nodes.rationale: No Jira webhooks, WebSockets, SSE, or Slack event subscriptions exist; the macOS app polls every 30s and cron checks run at minute precision. This keeps the system stateless on Vercel and means real-time upgrades can be added without breaking existing code.

nodes.label: LazyhandBar Polling Orchestration (TicketListViewModel)
nodes.rationale: Timer.scheduledTimer with configurable interval (default 30s from AppConfig.pollingInterval in ~/.lazyhand/config.json); detects new tickets by diffing fetched keys against a known set, then plays sound, shows banner, and updates the widget.

nodes.label: Jira Service Client (lib/services/jira.ts)
nodes.rationale: Uses HTTP Basic Auth (email:apiToken base64) against Jira REST v3 (search/jql, comments, transitions, attachments); transformIssue maps custom fields customfield_10451/10453/10400 to wlMainTicketType/wlSubTicketType/customerLevel and merges saved status/action from the DB.

nodes.label: Dynamic Trigger-Time Cron Scheduling
nodes.rationale: Vercel only supports one hard-coded cron (daily backup), so /api/cron?task=shift is hit every minute and compares the current Asia/Bangkok time against trigger_time_1 (17:10) and trigger_time_2 (22:40) stored in the app_settings table — letting users change shift times without redeploying.

nodes.label: Zod Environment Schema (lib/env.ts)
nodes.rationale: All env vars validated with Zod at startup (DATABASE_URL, JIRA_URL/EMAIL/API_TOKEN, SLACK_* tokens, GROQ/OPENAI keys, AI_PROVIDER default groq); getDatabaseConfig caps pool at 3 connections in prod for serverless.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Extract Services from API Routes
nodes.rationale: The 450-line ai-autofill route mixed AI logic, Jira calls, and prompt construction; extracting AIAutofillService, SlackMessagingService, and HandoverService shrinks routes to ~25-40 lines and restores the thin-route rule. Ranked highest priority for biggest impact.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1: extract services from api routes

nodes.label: Phase 2: Consolidate Database Layer
nodes.rationale: Two parallel DB access patterns coexist: legacy functional lib/services/database.ts (604 lines) and modern class-based server/repository. Rather than a breaking rewrite, database.ts becomes a ~100-line backward-compatible re-export layer delegating to TicketService/SettingsService.

nodes.label: Phase 5: Theme Config Separation
nodes.rationale: A single 1029-line theme-config.ts held all 7 themes; splitting into per-theme modules under lib/theme/themes/ with a THEME_CONFIGS map makes adding themes cheap and isolates maintenance.

nodes.label: Modular Theme System (lib/theme/themes)
nodes.rationale: Adding a theme touches 8 files in a fixed order: type union (lib/types), THEMES metadata (lib/constants), per-theme config file, THEME_CONFIGS registration, nav items, globals.css body/utility classes, theme-store localStorage validation, and an optional scene component.

nodes.label: Next.js Best Practices Guide (Serena Memory Copy)
nodes.norm_label: next.js best practices guide (serena memory copy)

nodes.label: Server Components First / Client at Leaves
nodes.rationale: Default to Server Components and push 'use client' to leaf components so static parts (headers, sidebars) never ship client JS; client components are reserved for interactivity, browser APIs, and hooks.
nodes.norm_label: server components first / client at leaves

nodes.label: Enforced Code Standards (File Size / Structure Rules)
nodes.rationale: Hard limits (routes 80, services 250, components 200, hooks 100, utils 150 lines; functions max 30 lines/4 params/3 nesting) keep files small enough for token-efficient AI navigation; a PostToolUse hook warns automatically so enforcement needs no manual review.
nodes.norm_label: enforced code standards (file size / structure rules)

nodes.label: Structural Navigation via Codemaps
nodes.rationale: Codemaps are read instead of source files to save tokens; update rule requires codemap changes in the same commit as code changes so the maps never drift.

nodes.label: Twelve-Factor App Methodology
nodes.rationale: Adopted for cloud-native deployments: env-var config via lib/env.ts (Factor III), stateless processes with state in PostgreSQL (Factor VI), stdout structured logging via lib/logger.ts (Factor XI), health checks at /api/health (Factor IX).

nodes.label: Modular Theme System
nodes.rationale: Themes are modular configs under lib/theme/themes/ with accessor functions in theme-config.ts, so new themes (7 exist: default, pixel, lunar, christmas, coding, clash, angkor_pixel) can be added without touching shared components.

nodes.label: PoW Challenge Authentication
nodes.rationale: Mutation endpoints are protected by a Proof-of-Work challenge (client solves nonce, sends x-challenge-session / x-challenge-solution headers) to deter bots without requiring user accounts; combined with rate limiting on sensitive endpoints.

nodes.label: TicketData Model
nodes.rationale: Core data store for handover info; keyed by Jira ticket_key for O(1) PK lookups since that is the sole access pattern.

nodes.label: AppSetting Model
nodes.rationale: Generic key-value store chosen so new settings (theme, memberMentions, triggerTimes, customChannel) need no schema migrations.

nodes.label: ScheduledComment Model
nodes.rationale: Cron-expression driven automated comments targeting either Jira or Slack; last_posted_at tracks execution.

nodes.label: Backup Model
nodes.rationale: Point-in-time JSONB snapshots of ticket_data, app_settings and scheduled_comments; auto backups run before significant operations, restore replaces all current data.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern (Data Access Layer)
nodes.rationale: All DB operations go through repository classes; services layer business logic on top, keeping API routes free of persistence details.

nodes.label: Sakura Theme
nodes.rationale: Visual direction: soft watercolor pink, edge-only floral decoration, floating petals, light-theme-first with the center 55-65% of the background kept visually quiet so table rows and inputs stay readable. The finish plan later chose repo-native CSS/SVG placeholders over downloading external assets, keeping theme plumbing intact so higher-fidelity bitmaps can swap in later.

nodes.label: claude-mem Codebase Indexing
nodes.rationale: Tree-sitter AST indexing into a persistent cross-session symbol database eliminates the re-explain-the-codebase tax: smart_search replaces reading 14 service files to find one method.

nodes.label: Codemaps (Static Structural Snapshots)
nodes.rationale: Three compact committed snapshot files replace reading 14 service files, 40+ route files, and 42 component files; deliberately manually maintained (not auto-generated) to stay simple and avoid a build-step dependency, with a same-commit update rule to prevent drift.

nodes.label: PostToolUse File-Size Hook
nodes.rationale: Non-blocking by explicit user choice (warnings only, Claude continues); bash script checks wc -l against per-path-pattern limits after every Write/Edit. Auto-running npm run build on Stop was rejected as too slow for a hook.

nodes.label: /feature Scaffolding Command
nodes.rationale: Replaces the 4-step manual /new-api flow with one command scaffolding a full vertical slice (schema + service + route + barrel export + codemap entries), enforcing conventions (thin routes, Zod validation, logger, apiSuccess helpers) from the start.
